::: {.why}
The second source of returns, and the one that pays for a service rather than for risk: you are being compensated for standing there, and charged by anyone who knows more than you.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the two costs a market maker's spread has to cover, and say which of the two a fast quote update reduces.
- Simulate one day of quoting and show how inventory risk moves your quotes even when your view has not changed.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Watch the Copenhagen microstructure lectures on dealer markets and the components of the spread. The decomposition into order-processing, inventory and adverse-selection costs is the framework you use again in week 42.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Simulate: a mid-price random walk, you quote one tick either side, you fill with some probability per side, and your inventory accumulates. Run 1,000 steps. Plot profit and inventory. Then add a rule that skews your quotes against your inventory and show what it does to the variance of the outcome.
:::
:::
